open.text: Second night. The fog has not moved. Neither, you realise, have you: you don't remember going home.
Evening, you. Sleep well? ...No. Me neither.
The staff photo is still turned to the wall. There is a second pin in it now.
...Tarrow ranger station. Thank you to the premises that stayed open. An update. They are learning. Some of them have the veins now. Some keep their reflections in time.
So look at the floor. Under the tubes a person throws one soft shadow, and it stays under them. None, or several, or one that moves by itself: do not serve.
And talk to them. They borrow. If they hand your own words back to you, or name a town that is not on your map, do not serve. Tarrow out.
Shadows now. They'll have us checking teeth by Friday.

hand.text: A bottle goes over while you restock the fridge. You reach into the broken glass without thinking.
A cut across the palm, deep. You look down to see how bad.
Wren has your wrist before you see anything. A tea towel, then a bandage from the first-aid tin, wound tight and fast, the way you'd wrap something to post it.

then.text: There. Good as new. Better. Don't pick at it.
You pull back the edge of the bandage. The cut is clean and deep and there is nothing in it. No red. Something pale and close-grained, like the inside of a mushroom.
I said don't. ...It'll have closed by morning. It always does.
Wren turns a hand over on the counter, palm up, like somebody paying by card. There are veins. They are silver, and they are not still.
Yours are the same. Under the bandage. I've known since the second night. I didn't want you to be frightened.
Wren is smiling. It is the first smile you have seen up here that is not held a moment too long. It is held exactly as long as yours.

knock.text: Half past one. From the storeroom: three knocks. Patient. Evenly spaced.

then.text: You rap the door three times. A pause. Then, from the other side, at the height of your own hand: three knocks back.
Don't do that again. Please. They get their hopes up.
No. Not tonight. Promise me something, Sam. It's just us. No matter what. Say it.
No. I didn't think you could. Not yet.
Good. It's nothing. It's only us in here.

storeroom.text: The storeroom again. Faster now: knocking that wants out.
Something is said in a voice you served coffee to. Then nothing is said.
Light. Wren, rinsing their hands in the mop sink.
That's the last one I do for you tonight.

intro: ...Tarrow ranger station, first-light report, second night. Fog unchanged. Road closed.
outro: Corrigan's Roadhouse: we have had no voice contact from you in three weeks, only the call-in tone. Somebody is pressing the button. Tarrow out.

epilogue.text: In the staff toilet you unwrap your hand. There is no cut. There is not even a line.
You don't unwrap your hand. You know what is under there, and what isn't.
Tomorrow's the last of the roster. Then it's just us. No more radio. I promise.
One more night on the roster. Try to stay with me for it.

summary.text: Most of the people who have come to your counter are still people.
Some of them made it down the mountain. You have stopped counting.
The fog is taking more than its share. A good part of that is you.
Wren walks you to the door at knock-off, and does not quite let you through it.
Wren watches you clock off, and says nothing, and keeps watching.
Wren counts the till twice and looks at you three times.
Your hands are steady. You check them twice anyway.
Your reflection in the door glass takes a moment to catch you up.
You say goodnight to your reflection. It says it first.
